title: Types of work
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:12Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-20T12:25:40Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point covers paid, unpaid, full-time, part-time and casual work at a Year 7 depth, but it does not teach the employee versus self-employed distinction the brief requires, and that addition is a new idea rather than a small change.

draft.title: Types of work
card: Paid work earns money, such as wages or income from a business. Unpaid work is done without pay, such as volunteering at a surf life saving club or caring for a family member.

Full-time workers have regular hours, usually around 38 a week. Part-time workers have regular but fewer hours. Casual workers have no guaranteed hours and are usually paid a higher hourly rate, called a loading.
An employee works for an employer, who pays them and sets their tasks and hours.
A self-employed person runs their own business. They earn income from customers, not wages from an employer, and make their own decisions about their work.
draft.remember: Work can be paid or unpaid. Paid work can be full-time, part-time or casual, as an employee or self-employed.

a.q: Jo works at a shop for an employer. She has no guaranteed hours and is paid a loading on her hourly rate. What type of worker is she?
a.why: Jo has no guaranteed hours and works for an employer, so she is a casual employee. A part-time employee has regular hours, so that option is tempting but does not fit.
a.clue: Look at whether her hours are guaranteed.

b.q: Priya mows lawns in Bathurst. She owns her mower, finds her own customers and sets her own prices and hours. How is her work best described?
opts: Paid work, as a self-employed person
Paid work, as a casual employee
Paid work, as a part-time employee
b.why: Priya earns income from customers and makes her own decisions, so she is self-employed. A casual employee also has irregular hours, but works for an employer who sets the tasks and pays wages, and Priya has no employer.
b.clue: Who decides her prices and hours, and who pays her?

b.best: Paid work, as a self-employed person
